analysis: For the contracted dense arrays of finite numbers, the replacement preserves behavior: it allocates a fresh array, iterates values in order, appends each value multiplied by two, and never writes to the input. Empty inputs produce a fresh empty array. Both implementations use the same multiplication operation, including its behavior for signed zero and overflow. Sparse arrays and custom iterators are explicitly excluded, so differences concerning those inputs do not establish regressions. The names r and x are less descriptive than the repository preference, but that preference is advisory and does not affect correctness. No behavioral defects were identified.
coverage: Read every snapshot input: contract, diff, provenance, discovery instructions, verification template and challenge template. Inspected change.mjs at both exact pinned commits with git show, inspected head commit metadata and its root tree, and confirmed the head contains no additional files or callers requiring examination.
limitations: Source review only; project execution and executable checks were excluded by the request.
